newsitem.title: USA: AMR pilots could consider compromise - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: AMR pilots could consider compromise - WSJ.

text.p: Directors of the union representing American Airlines' pilots would consider compromising on a key issue if the carrier raises it financial offer to the pilots, the Wall Street Journal said Tuesday.

People close to the negotiations told the paper that just before the strike was called, the board for the Allied Pilots' Association eased its demand that its members fly regional jets, which American wants to fly with commuter pilots who are paid less. Meanwhile, American moved closer to the pilots' demands for pay raises at least matching cost of living increases, the report said.
"Both sides saw each other willing to go over the edge, and that was a revelation," one person involved from the union side told the paper.
However union President James Sovich told the paper he still considers a strike likely.
The report said a hypothetical deal arranged by mediators late Friday was accepted by American president Donald Carty and some union directors, but not a majority.
